nameless-heading-element/case-01.mechanism: The fourth section's heading (h2#h-nutri) contains only an icon-font glyph at the Private Use Area codepoint U+F080, painted as a bar-chart icon. The codepoint is non-whitespace so empty-heading does not fire, but U+F080 has no Unicode/CLDR name, so the heading's accessible name is an unpronounceable glyph that conveys no section name. The visible 'Nutrition' meaning lives only in the icon, which AT cannot name.
nameless-heading-element/case-01.scenario: Vegetable recipe page (Ember & Root, 'Slow-roast harissa carrots'). The About/Ingredients/Method sections carry text h2s (with the icon as an aria-hidden accent); the final nutrition section's h2#h-nutri holds only the bar-chart icon-font glyph U+F080 with no text, so it appears in the heading list as a nameless level-2 heading.
nameless-heading-element/case-01.note: Same nameless-heading defect, but the page and mechanism drifted: the prose describes a GOV.UK residential-parking-permit page whose 'Fees and payment' h2#sec-fees holds a single non-breaking space (U+00A0); the real page is a carrots recipe whose nameless heading is a PUA icon-font glyph (U+F080), and the selector is h2#h-nutri, not h2#sec-fees.

nameless-heading-element/case-03.mechanism: The Method section's heading (h2#h-method) contains only a decorative dashed-rule divider image whose alt was auto-filled with the uploaded file name ('divider-line-ornament-2x.png'). Because the alt is non-empty, empty-heading and image-alt both pass, but the computed accessible name is a meaningless asset filename, not a section name, so the cooking-instructions section is announced by a filename and conveys no purpose.
nameless-heading-element/case-03.scenario: Recipe page (The Weeknight Larder, 'Slow-Braised Short Rib Ragu'). Before-you-start / Ingredients / To serve sections use text h2s; the Method section's h2#h-method holds only a decorative dashed-rule divider whose alt is the file name, so the heading exposes a junk filename instead of 'Method'.
nameless-heading-element/case-03.note: Same image-only nameless-heading defect, but the concrete instance drifted: the prose describes a wedding microsite ('Priya & Daniel') whose 'Travel & Stay' h2#h-travel holds a decorative swirl (empty alt, accessible name ''); the real page is a recipe whose Method heading uses a divider image with a non-empty filename alt, and the selector is h2#h-method, not h2#h-travel.
